title: Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance
description: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance to join our Compliance team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: The Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance supports the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will provide leadership over key compliance functions, including regulatory compliance, regulatory change management/implementation, compliance operations, investigations, monitoring and auditing, policy governance, and compliance education. You will anticipate regulatory and industry developments, translates them into enterprise compliance priorities, and partners with cross-functional leaders to identify and mitigate compliance risks, strengthen internal controls, and promote a culture of ethics and integrity. You will exercise significant independent judgment, develops a compliance organization, and serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders on complex healthcare regulatory matters. You will report into the Vice President, Chief Compliance Officer. Work Location: This position is based in our New York City office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $218,592 - $286,902 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Lead the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program, including the multi-year compliance strategy, annual compliance work plans, risk assessments, policy governance, regulatory change management/implementation, monitoring, auditing, and reporting activities. Translate enterprise compliance priorities into an relevant operating plan; establish ownership and governance; allocate resources; develop compliance managers and team members; remove barriers; and lead accountability for measurable outcomes. Anticipate regulatory and industry developments and advise senior leaders on their possible effects for Oscar's products, market participation, business strategy, and operating model. Provide guidance on federal and state healthcare regulations, contractual obligations, and emerging regulatory risks across applicable lines of business. Oversee compliance investigations, hotline reporting, the Special Investigations Unit, fraud-prevention activities, corrective action plans, and remediation efforts, ensuring timely resolution and appropriate escalation of significant compliance concerns. Partner with leaders across Legal, Privacy, Security, Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk, Clinical, Product, Operations, and People teams to embed compliance requirements into business processes and strategic initiatives. Set and uphold enterprise standards for ethics and compliance by leading education, communications, and awareness initiatives that strengthen Oscar's culture of ethics and compliance. Lead compliance reporting and engagement for executive leadership, Compliance Committee, Board committees, and regulatory examinations; support interactions with regulators and external auditors. Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations Other duties as assigned Requirements: 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare compliance, regulatory affairs, legal compliance, audit, or enterprise risk management. 5+ years leading high-performing compliance teams and enterprise-wide compliance initiatives. Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and maintaining an effective healthcare compliance program aligned with OIG Compliance Program Guidance and applicable federal and state regulations. Experience supporting highly regulated healthcare organizations, including health plans, managed care organizations, healthcare technology companies, provider organizations, or related entities. Track record of anticipating regulatory developments and translating them into enterprise priorities, operating plans, and business controls. Demonstrated experience leading complex compliance investigations, monitoring and auditing activities, regulatory risk assessments, corrective action planning, and policy governance. Experience advising senior business leaders on complex regulatory and operational compliance issues and leading their resolution Strong written and verbal communication skills, experience presenting to executive leadership, governance committees, regulators, or external auditors. title: Vice President, Data Governance
description: Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries. The Vice President, Data Governance leads Experian North America's Data Governance and Privacy Operations function. This role owns two connected mandates: advancing North America's data governance maturity through enterprise-wide data cataloging, lineage, and access-approval capabilities; and running the day-to-day operations of our Privacy Framework, including consumer rights requests, the consumer privacy portal, and the Privacy Monitoring program. The role reports to the leader of our Data Office, and leads a team of data stewards and privacy professionals and partners closely with Legal, Compliance, IT, and business unit leaders across North America. At Experian, we believe great work happens when people come together. We're focused on attracting talent in and around our designated hub locations who are open to collaborating with colleagues in person. Aligning employees to these talent markets helps foster collaboration, strengthen team connections, and support long-term career growth within Experian. You will reside in or near one of our collaboration hubs: Costa Mesa, CA; San Jose, CA; Allen, TX; Austin, TX; Franklin, TN; New York, NY; Schaumberg, IL; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta, GA; Boston, MA; Seattle, WA Key Responsibilities Define and execute the multi-year roadmap to advance Experian NA's data governance maturity, setting measurable milestones and reporting progress to senior leadership. Lead the design, build, and rollout of a NA-wide Data Catalog and Data Lineage platform, partnering with IT and data engineering on architecture, implementation and adoption. Establish and improve data governance policies, standards, and operating procedures (data quality, metadata management, data classification) across NA business units. Design and enhance the process by which teams request and are granted approval for data access, balancing business agility with risk and compliance requirements. Own the end-to-end daily operations of Experian's Privacy Framework for NA, ensuring consistent, compliant execution across all programs. Oversee timely and accurate response to consumer privacy requests (access, deletion, correction, opt-out) in line with applicable regulations (e.g., CCPA/CPRA, state privacy laws) and internal SLAs. Manage and continuously improve the consumer-facing privacy portal, ensuring a seamless, compliant consumer experience and resolving operational or technical issues. Direct the Privacy Monitoring program, including ongoing risk assessments, control testing, issue tracking, and remediation across NA. Mentor and manage a team of data stewards and privacy professionals, setting goals, developing talent, and ensuring adequate coverage and succession planning. Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Compliance, Security, IT, and business leaders to align data governance and privacy operations with regulatory requirements and business objectives. Develop and report key metrics and dashboards (KPIs/KRIs) on data governance maturity, access approvals, consumer request turnaround, and privacy monitoring findings for executive stakeholders. 12+ years of progressive experience in data governance, data management, or privacy operations, including 5+ years in a people-leadership role. Demonstrated success building or scaling enterprise data governance programs, including data catalog, metadata management, and data lineage initiatives. Hands-on experience with data catalog/lineage platforms (e.g., Collibra, Alation, Informatica, etc.) and data governance tooling. Deep working knowledge of U.S. privacy and data protection regulations (CCPA/CPRA, state privacy laws, GLBA, FCRA) and their operational implications. Experience designing or operating consumer rights request processes and consumer-facing privacy portals at scale. Experience running a privacy monitoring or compliance testing program, including risk assessment, control design, and issue remediation. Strong understanding of data access governance models, including approval workflows, role-based access, and data risk classification. Experience leading and developing a team of data stewards, analysts, or privacy professionals, including performance management and talent development. Strong program and change management skills, with the ability to drive adoption of new governance processes and platforms across a large, matrixed organization. Experience shaping organizational strategy through financial, market, and performance analysis; building business cases and assessing decisions' P&L and long-term impact. title: Principal - Accounting Platform
description: BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com . This role requires being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.  If you have spent your career in SOX, internal controls, audit, controllership, or financial close, and you want to build the systems that fix what you find instead of only testing them, this role is for you. Why this role exists  Every product BitGo ships eventually becomes a number: a balance, a fee, a statement, a journal entry, a regulatory filing. As a public company and a federally chartered trust bank, we have to prove those numbers are right every period, across many products, legal entities, and jurisdictions.  You will own the product strategy for the financial and accounting platform that makes those numbers right by construction, as we add products, entities, and asset types. You will turn accounting requirements into scalable, auditable, self-service platform capabilities that product, engineering, finance, and compliance can build on.  Digital assets make this harder, and more interesting, than it is at a traditional bank. On chain activity, custody structures, staking, tokenized assets, and settlement each move through our systems differently, and each has to land correctly on the books. The industry is still writing the playbook for much of this. You will help write it.  Level  We are hiring at Senior or Principal level, depending on experience. The core scope is the same at both. At Principal, you have already set platform strategy, led accounting systems, or established control standards that multiple teams adopted, and you will own the crossproduct standards and the working relationship with finance and audit leadership with more independence from day one. Two paths to this role  There is more than one way to be great at this job. You may come from product management and built financial compliance platforms. You may come from audit, controllership, or accounting systems and have spent years finding where numbers break, and then built the thing that fixed it. We are just as interested in the second group. If you are an auditor or accountant with a builder mindset, you will be evaluated on the same scope and the same bar as a product manager. What matters is that you have shipped: tools, automation, control frameworks, or systems that other teams adopted and kept using. What you will own  The financial data and accounting platform roadmap: Define and deliver the shared capabilities that make financial data trustworthy by construction: ledger and sub-ledger integrity, balance and activity reconciliation, fee and revenue calculation, client reporting, and the feeds into the general ledger and the financial close.  Controls built into the product: Partner with finance, internal audit, and external auditors to turn SOX and internal control requirements into product capabilities instead of manual procedures. When a control needs a build, you own the requirements, the plan, and the timeline, delivered in step with the audit calendar.  Platform standards across products and entities: Make sure new products, new asset types, new legal entities, and acquisitions plug into the platform instead of creating bespoke accounting workarounds. You set the standards, interfaces, and data contracts that product teams build against.  Regulatory and audit readiness: Work with compliance, legal, and risk so the platform supports regulatory reporting, books-and-records requirements, and examiner and auditor requests. You run dated plans against external deadlines and flag early when a timeline is at risk.  Close, reporting, and operational efficiency:   Reduce the manual effort, elapsed time, and risk in month-end and quarter-end close. Establish the metrics that show whether the platform is working: reconciliation breaks, close duration, audit adjustments, manual journal volume, and time to onboard a new product.  What success looks like in the first two quarters  A documented map of how each major product's financial activity reaches the general ledger, with manual steps and gaps identified and prioritized.  A dated platform roadmap agreed with finance, engineering, and comp

title: Manager / Senior Manager, Financial Crime Compliance Testing (CONTRACT)
description: At Broadridge, we've built a culture where the highest goal is to empower others to accomplish more. If you’re passionate about developing your career, while helping others along the way, come join the Broadridge team. Broadridge is Growing. We are seeking a Senior Manager to support financial crime compliance testing and quality assurance across anti-money laundering (AML), sanctions, and related compliance programs. In this role, you will assess whether controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively, identify gaps and emerging risks, and communicate clear, evidence-based findings to stakeholders. The successful candidate brings hands-on experience in compliance testing, monitoring, or internal audit, along with the judgment to turn test results into practical recommendations and audit-ready reporting. Key Responsibilities: · Plan and execute risk-based testing and quality assurance reviews across financial crime compliance controls, including AML and sanctions. · Assess control design and operating effectiveness against applicable requirements, internal policies, procedures, and risk frameworks. · Develop or refine test objectives, procedures, sampling approaches, evidence requests, and documentation standards. · Review records, process documentation, and other supporting evidence; document work clearly enough to support independent review. · Identify control weaknesses, coverage gaps, recurring issues, and potential root causes; evaluate the significance of findings. · Prepare concise, audit-ready reports that explain the scope, methodology, evidence, results, and recommended actions. · Discuss findings with business and compliance stakeholders, validate factual accuracy, and support timely resolution of questions. · Track remediation commitments and assess whether corrective actions adequately address identified issues. · Summarize themes and trends to help stakeholders strengthen financial crime risk management and control performance. · Manage review activities and deliverables, coordinating with relevant partners to keep work on schedule. Required Qualifications and Experience: · Proven experience conducting AML or sanctions compliance testing, monitoring, or internal audits. · Solid understanding of financial crime risk management frameworks and the role of controls in mitigating risk. · Demonstrated ability to evaluate control effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and assess the significance of issues. · Experience preparing clear, well-supported test documentation and audit-ready reports. · Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and sound professional judgment. · Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain findings to varied stakeholders. · Ability to organize multiple review activities and meet agreed deadlines. Preferred Qualifications · Experience working across compliance, risk, audit, or financial services environments. · Relevant professional certification or training in compliance, financial crime, risk management, or internal audit. · Experience supporting remediation tracking or assessing corrective actions. · Experience leading review work or coordinating the contributions of other team members, particularly for Senior Manager-level candidates. #LI-MR1 #LI-Hybrid We are dedicated to fostering a collaborative, engaging, and inclusive environment and are committed to providing a workplace that empowers associates to be authentic and bring their best to work. We believe that associates do their best when they feel safe, understood, and valued, and we work diligently and collaboratively to ensure Broadridge is a company—and ultimately a community—that recognizes and celebrates everyone’s unique perspective. Use of AI in Hiring As part of the recruiting process, Broadridge may use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools, to help review and evaluate applications. These tools are used only to support our recruiters and hiring managers, and all employment decisions include human review to ensure fairness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable laws. Please note that honesty and transparency are critical to our hiring process. Any attempt to falsify, misrepresent, or disguise information in an application, resume, assessment, or interview will result in disqualification from consideration.

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. In this role, you will be a hands-on technical contributor and key executor of our IT SOX compliance program, with deep focus on our IT General Controls, IT Application Controls, and system risk assessments. This role reports to the Head of IT SOX and is well-suited for someone who is comfortable with ambiguity, thrives in a high-pace environment, and enjoys solving problems that don't yet have industry-standard answers. This is a high-impact opportunity to collaborate with first and second lines of defense to help establish a control environment suitable for an AI-first company! title: Investment Governance Manager
description: About Invesco As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description About the Team The Investment Governance team is responsible for the first-line governance framework that provides for oversight of the investment lifecycle, operating standards, incident management and effective risk mitigation across Invesco’s global investment platform. The team partners with Investments, Capital Markets, Front Office Operations and LCAR functions to strengthen first-line processes, improve decision-making, ensure appropriate escalation, reporting and oversight. About the Role The role supports the design, implementation and ongoing operation of Invesco’s global investment governance framework. This includes the development of robust governance documentation and decision-useful management information, advising governance bodies on potential enhancements to ensure appropriate oversight of risks, coordinating investment incident management and reporting processes, analyzing investment lifecycle events and developing operational playbooks to mitigate risk. Working across Investments, Capital Markets, Front Office Operations and the three lines of defense, the role promotes a multi-layered investment governance approach in support of the delivery of good client outcomes. The position reports to the Global Head of Investment Governance. Responsibilities of the Role Provide first-line ownership of investment-related policies, standards, procedures, and guidance. Coordinate the intake, assessment, triage, escalation, and governance of investment and trading incidents. Ensure consistency of incident records to support better management information and reporting. Track incident remediation plans, accountable owners, and deadlines, and support the delivery of remediation plans within the first line. Map investment lifecycle activities and material risks across relevant asset classes and develop playbooks and checklists to support effective risk management and improved decision-making. Produce management information, dashboards, and committee reporting on a variety of governance topics. Coordinate engagement with Legal, Compliance, Audit, Risk and Controls Assurance on governance topics and investment process enhancements. Support the Global Head of Investment Governance on the execution of investment governance initiatives arising out of the design and implementation of Invesco’s global investment governance framework. Requirements for the Role Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, accounting, business, risk management, law or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Typically, five or more years of relevant experience in asset management, investment operations, investment risk, operational risk, governance and controls, compliance, internal audit or front-office business management. Strong knowledge of the investment lifecycle, including portfolio management, order generation, trading, post-trade activities, investment data and support processes. Experience drafting and maintaining investment, trading, risk or control policies and procedures and supporting audit, assurance or governance reviews. Strong organizational, analytical and communication skills, with experience producing clear papers, management information, dashboards and senior-management reporting. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Familiarity with investment data, order management systems, operational resilience or regulatory change is advantageous. Relevant professional qualification, or progress towards one, such as CFA, FRM, CAIA, CIA, CPA, CISA or an equivalent credential, is preferred.
